tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

device-mrr-geometry: Section II, p.2: the paper states the 300-nm TFLN wafer, 180-nm etch, R = 40 um, simulated ng = 2.4038 and the 0.98-nm FSR 'by design'. Read in context; it is the device design, not a measurement.
lamp-setup: Section III, p.3-4: potassium HCL (Ne fill, Appendix C) at 8 mA and 280 V, SPCM detector, 1-s integration per point. Read in context. The 8 mA point is the detection run; the lamp current is later scanned 8-40 mA for the linewidth study.
one-line-at-a-time: Section III p.3 and Section VI p.7: the 3.4-nm doublet spacing lets only one line pass the MRR at a time, and the authors say the doublet was measured individually with one chip. Both clauses are limits of this demonstration that the authors state.
model-assumptions: Section IV, Eq. 6 and text, p.5: the paper states its computational inputs: weakly ionized plasma, local thermal equilibrium, g1/g0 = 4, 21.56454 eV, n = 1.61e23 m^-3 from p = 5 torr at 300 K. These are its stated inputs, even though g1/g0 and the energy are cited constants.
chip-structure-two-ppln-one-lossy: Section 2, p.2: the paper states the z-cut 600-nm TFLN wafer, two 4-mm PPLN waveguides (a, b) and a lossy central waveguide (c). Note: the Fig. 1 caption says 'three PPLN waveguides', a loose wording in the paper; the text and the reference-waveguide note agree with the value.
cr-strip-loss-reservoir: Section 2 p.2 and Fig. 1 caption p.3: the paper states that the Cr strip over the middle waveguide introduces the loss rate gamma. This is how the device is built.
waveguide-geometry-and-poling-period: Fig. 1(b) caption p.3 and Supplementary S1 p.1: the paper states the cross-section parameters, the 4-mm length, the 3.25-um poling period and the simulated indices n775 = 2.1262, n1550 = 1.8875 used for the QPM design. All are design values the authors state.
fabrication-poling-and-cr-strip: Section 5 Methods, Periodic Poling and Cr strip, p.12: the paper states 60 cycles of 480-V pulses and the Cr strip (250 nm wide, 20 nm thick) on the 100-nm SiO2 cladding above the central waveguide. Fabrication protocol as stated.
hamiltonian-spdc-and-weak-pump-in-c: Section 2, Eqs. 1-3, p.4: the paper states what its model covers: SPDC in a and b, nonlinear terms in c dropped by assumption (pump in c ~ 0), c modes from linear hopping. The value frames this as an assumption the paper makes, which is what the text says.
adiabatic-elimination-condition-and-gamm: Section 2, Eq. 4, p.4: the paper defines the effective Hamiltonian and Gamma = |kappa|^2/gamma and states the condition gamma >> |kappa| for its elimination. HIGH covers the definition and the stated condition only. The elimination procedure itself is cited from [57], not derived here. Check: 76.62^2/813 = 7.22 cm^-1 matches S1.
hermitian-coherent-reference-system: Section 2, Eq. 9, p.5: the paper defines the reference coherent system by Hc = HNL + Gamma sum(a_mu^dagger b_mu + h.c.). It matches S4.
master-equation-versus-nhh-definition: Section 2, Eqs. 5-8, p.5: the paper defines the two simulation methods and rewrites the master equation as the NHH term plus the jump term 2 gamma sum c rho c^dagger, which the NHH method drops. I checked the algebra: -i(Heff rho - rho Heff^dagger) gives -Gamma{O^dagger O, rho} and matches Eq. 5. The monitoring interpretation is the standard meaning of the jump term.
simulation-parameters-and-truncation: Section 2, p.6: the paper states g*eps = 6.93 /m, Gamma = 7.22 /cm and Nmax = 10. These agree with Methods (g*eps) and S1 (Gamma).
g4-and-inter-pair-ratio-r4-definition: Section 2, Eqs. 10-11, p.5 and Section 3 p.9: the paper defines R(4) = g(4)/(g_a(2) g_b(2)). For independent pairs g(4) factorizes, so the baseline R(4) = 1 follows from the definition.
three-photon-ratio-r3-definition: Section 3, p.10: the paper defines R(3) as the three-fold correlation over the product of the pair's two-photon correlation and the mean photon number of the third mode. The formula is in the text.
bright-dark-supermode-basis: Section 2 p.6 and S2 Eq. S3: the paper defines B = (a+b)/sqrt2, D = (a-b)/sqrt2 and states the transformation is canonical. Checked: [B,B^dagger] = 1.
co-and-cross-generation-amplitudes: Section 2 after Eq. 17, p.7: Lambda_co = g*eps e^{i theta/2} cos(theta/2), Lambda_x = i g*eps e^{i theta/2} sin(theta/2). This follows from Eq. 12. Note: S2 prints Lambda_co with e^{i theta} (no /2), which does not match Eq. 12; it is a likely typo in the supplement. The value follows the main text, which is the consistent form.
dark-mode-exact-dfs-of-dissipator: Section 2, Eq. 13, p.7: the paper shows the master equation in the B/D basis with only D[B_mu] in the dissipator, so the dark operators drop out. I checked it: with aµ+bµ = sqrt2 Bµ, 2Gamma D[sqrt2 B] = 4Gamma D[B]. The derivation is one substitution and is not written out, so the coordinator may downgrade it. The scope is the dissipator only, as the next sentence of the paper says.
spdc-pump-and-temperature-setup: Fig. 4 caption, p.8: the paper states the 775.4-nm CW pump with FPC through the FWDM and 69 C chip temperature with +/-3 mK TEC stability. Methods repeats it.
filters-and-detector-setup: Section 5 Methods, Experiment Details, p.13: the paper states the two LP filters (140 dB total), the two DWDM filters (125 GHz, centered 1549.35 and 1552.54 nm) and SNSPDs (85%, 50-100 Hz dark). The detector figures are the stated specs of the setup.
du-2026-fiber-chip-coupling-loss: Section 5 Methods, Experiment Details, p.13: the lensed fiber (2-um MFD) gives 5 dB coupling loss per facet, as the paper states for its setup.
virtual-channel-fourfold-detection: Section 3, p.8: the paper states its protocol: virtual channel 1 from (as, ai) twofolds, virtual channel 2 from (bs, bi), and the coincidence between them.
r4-from-car4-binning: Fig. 5 caption p.9 and Section 3 p.9: the paper defines how R(4) is measured, as CAR(4) from coincidences summed over two 80-ns bins over summed accidentals. The equivalence is stated as the paper's operational definition. The value is framed as what the authors state.
coherent-comparison-is-numerical: Fig. 5 caption, p.9: the paper states the Hermitian comparison curve is a numerical prediction at the same 4-mm length, not a measurement.
four-photon-visibility-definition: Section 3, p.9: V = (Gmax - Gmin)/(Gmax + Gmin) for the fourfold correlation, as the paper defines it. The 94% and 99% values are not part of this item.
pump-amplitude-and-pair-generation-stren: Section 5 Methods, p.12: the paper states the undepleted classical pump, the 4 mW on-chip power and the resulting eps = 6.41e-10 and g*eps = 6.93 /m as its model inputs. I checked the arithmetic: lambda P/(8 pi c) gives about 6.4e-10, and 1.08e10 x 6.41e-10 = 6.92.
integration-time-and-g4-estimator: Section 5 Methods, Eq. 21, p.13: the paper defines the experimental g(4) estimator (counts over R1R2R3R4 T and the three window widths) and states T = 30 min total integration time.
negligible-detuning-and-unbroken-regime: S1 p.2-3: the paper assumes detuning ~ 0 for identical waveguides a and b and states that, with Gamma > Delta, the four-photon correlation is studied in the anti-PT unbroken regime. This is the regime the paper states it covers.
mmi-design-lengths: S1, Fig. S2, p.3: the paper states the EME-optimized MMI dimensions LMMI = 34 um and Lt = 10 um for the 1x2 splitter of the MZI. These are the design parameters it uses.
coherent-system-analytic-phase-zero: S2, Eqs. S3-S13, p.4-5: the paper gives the linear equations of motion, the explicit solution (S10-S11) for theta = 0 with Gamma > g*eps, and the derived mean photon number and G(4). It checks both against simulation (Fig. S3). I spot-checked the eigenfrequency Omega and the x^4 small-z limit. The solution is stated, not derived step by step. The coordinator may downgrade it.
coherent-system-analytic-phase-pi: S2, Eqs. S14-S16, p.5: for theta = pi (Lambda_co = 0, Lambda_x = -g*eps) the paper gives the solution and <n> = sinh^2(g*eps z). I checked that S^4C^4 + 2S^6C^2 + S^8 = sinh^4 cosh^2(2 g*eps z). Checked against simulation in Fig. S3(b). The solution is stated, not derived step by step.
pump-not-adiabatically-eliminated-limit: S4, p.12: the paper states that gamma775 >> kappa775 is not met, so the classical pump sees roughly three coupled waveguides and the outputs show complementary phase tuning curves, not equal powers. It is a caveat about its own device at the pump wavelength. Both clauses describe that limitation.
recruit-tv-ad-mef-setup: Section 'Right User, Right Time, Right Message', p.1: the case story states the problem it addresses (reach viewers to the MEF, defined as the tipping point) and Recruit's aim. HIGH only for what the document states as its problem and the term MEF it defines. It is vendor material, and that the tipping-point effect is real is not established here.
recruit-project-transferred-note: Footnote, p.1: the document states that the project was transferred to Recruit Co.,Ltd. It is the document's own note on attribution.
dwave-production-application-definition: Introduction, p.1: 'Here, a production application means one that is actively being used by customers in a live environment...' is a definition the document gives for its own term.
dwave-pfg-scheduling-constraints: Pattison Food Group section, p.2 (continues over the page break): the document lists the scheduling constraints (stores a driver can reach, drivers per shift, at least 10 hours between shifts) as the problem setup. Vendor case material. HIGH only for what the document says the problem involves.

theory_low.temperature-retrieval-method: Section IV, Eqs. 3, 4, 8, p.5: this is the authors' retrieval model, not a proved result. The Voigt FWHM formula (Eq. 8) is an empirical approximation cited from [39], and the Lorentzian-sum rule is not proved here. No theorem or proof.
theory_low.collision-dominance-in-lamp: Appendix C, Fig. 11(e), p.9: an outcome of the authors' plasma model, read from a figure. It is a model result, not proved. 'K-Ne+ ignored as weaker' is an assertion without calculation.
theory_low.wildfire-model-crossover: Appendix E, Fig. 13, p.10: numerical outcome of the authors' wildfire model (5910 K, 5070 K). The 2500 K flaming limit is cited from [10]. A model result and a cited fact, not a proved result.
theory_low.heater-efficiency-model: Section IV p.6, Fig. 8: dneff/dT = 1.79e-5 /K is an FDTD simulation value and the 300-557 K range is extracted from fitted heater efficiency and Eq. 9. Simulated and fitted results, not proved. No derivation of the range is shown.
theory_low.anti-pt-symmetry-of-reduced-hamiltonian: Section 2, p.4: the anticommutation {PT, HL'} = 0 is asserted. The paper does not define the P and T operators and does not show the anticommutation. 'For Gamma >> g*eps the SPDC term is a perturbation' is a regime claim, also not shown. No proof in the paper, so not a proved result.
theory_low.phase-matching-hermitian-oscillation-vs-: Fig. 3 and Section 2, p.6-7: a numerical result for one parameter set with a physical argument (extra propagation phases vs dark and bright modes). The anti-PT claim holds under Gamma >> g*eps. A simulation outcome and an interpretation, not a proved result.
theory_low.dfs-limit-not-strict-liouvillian: Section 2, p.7: the first sentence (exact DFS of the dissipator, not a strict DFS of the full Liouvillian) is a stated limit. The second (collective loss purifies toward the dark manifold as a global attractor) is an interpretation with no derivation or simulation shown. The value bundles both. If split, the first would be HIGH on stated limit.
theory_low.bright-decay-rate-dark-protected: Section 2, Eqs. 14-17, p.7: the equations of motion are given without derivation. Eqs. 16-17 contain source terms from SPDC, and 'significantly longer lifetime' is an interpretation under Gamma >> g*eps. The 4 Gamma bright rate is consistent with Eq. 13, but there is no theorem or proof.
theory_low.master-equation-vs-nhh-photon-number-dis: Fig. 3 caption p.6 and Section 2 p.7: a numerical comparison at three phases for one parameter set, with the jump terms given as the cause. A simulation result, not proved.
theory_low.master-equation-needed-for-g4-nhh-ok-for: Section 2 p.7 and S3 p.9-10: a numerical comparison (Fig. S4) with a qualitative reason. No bound or proof. The paper says R(4) is 'largely unaffected', which is an empirical statement.
theory_low.quantum-jump-mechanism-g4-underestimated: S3, Figs. S5-S6, p.10-11: an explanatory argument backed by simulated figures. The paper does not derive it formally, and 'unphysical correlation' is its interpretation. Not a proved result.
theory_low.bright-dark-pair-mechanism-for-phase-dep: Section 3, p.10-11: a qualitative explanation set against one experiment, with no quantitative fit. An interpretation by the authors, not a proved result.
theory_low.nonlinear-coefficient-analytical-value: Section 5 Methods, Eqs. 18-19, p.12: zeta, Aeff and g come from a mode solver (FDE) and a formula cited from [58]. A computed design value, compared with one measurement (g_exp = 9.18e9). Not proved. Check: g*eps = 1.08e10 x 6.41e-10 = 6.92 /m.
theory_low.coupling-design-numbers-s1: S1, p.1-2: mode-solver (EME/FDE) simulation values for Lbeat, kappa, gamma and Gamma. Simulated design values, not measured and not proved. Note Gamma = 7.22 /cm uses the 1550-nm kappa and gamma (76.62^2/813).
theory_low.pump-weak-coupling-to-central-waveguide: S1 p.2: 'kappa1550 >> kappa775 ensures the pump in waveguide c is negligible' is asserted. The ratio compares two wavelengths and does not show the pump in c is small. S4 p.12 says the classical pump behaves approximately as three evanescently coupled waveguides, since gamma775 >> kappa775 is not met. That weakens 'negligible'. The model assumption itself is covered by the Hamiltonian-scope item.
theory_low.antipt-semi-analytical-gaussian-assumpti: S2 p.8-9: the method (semi-analytical, Gaussian state assumed) is a stated approximation. But the value also reports 'excellent agreement' with full simulation, which is a simulation outcome that the paper only shows in a figure. The value bundles a stated limit with a result. If split, the method and assumption clause would be HIGH on stated limit.
theory_low.antipt-mean-photon-number-phase-zero: S2 Eqs. S26-S27, p.7: the formula is damaged in the text layer (flattened fraction and exponents), the vacuum-noise term is only in part legible, and its derivation is not shown. It is not safe to grade as a proved result.
